Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin masturbārī.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mas.tuʁˈba(ʁ)/ [mas.tuɦˈba(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mas.tuʁˈba(ʁ)/ [mas.tuɦˈba(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /mas.tuɾˈba(ɾ)/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /maʃ.tuʁˈba(ʁ)/ [maʃ.tuʁˈba(χ)]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /mas.tuɻˈba(ɻ)/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐʃ.tuɾˈbaɾ/ [mɐʃ.tuɾˈβaɾ]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐʃ.tuɾˈbaɾ/ [mɐʃ.tuɾˈβaɾ]
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐʃ.tuɾˈba.ɾi/ [mɐʃ.tuɾˈβa.ɾi]

  • Hyphenation: mas‧tur‧bar

Verb

[edit]

masturbar (first-person singular present masturbo, first-person singular preterite masturbei, past participle masturbado)

  1. (reflexive) to masturbate (manually stimulate one's sexual organs)
    O rapaz masturbava-se todas as noites. ― The young man masturbated every night.
    Masturbo-me por prazer. ― I masturbate for pleasure.
  2. (transitive) to masturbate (manually stimulate someone else's sexual organs)
    Um parceiro masturba o outro. ― One partner masturbates the other.

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin masturbārī.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /mastuɾˈbaɾ/ [mas.t̪uɾˈβ̞aɾ]
  • Rhymes: -aɾ
  • Syllabification: mas‧tur‧bar

Verb

[edit]

masturbar (first-person singular present masturbo, first-person singular preterite masturbé, past participle masturbado)

  1. (transitive) to masturbate
  2. (reflexive) to masturbate oneself

Usage notes

[edit]
  • If the verb is used on oneself, the reflexive pronoun "me" must be added before the conjugated form of masturbar.
    Compare:
    Yo me masturbo. ― I masturbate (myself).
    Yo masturbo... ― I masturbate... (someone else).
